liebermann.notes: After Geoffrey of Monmouth, an originally separate volume in two hands of c. 1225: the first writes the Quadripartitus from Arg. 1 (Cnut, Alfred–Ine, Æthelstan, Edgar, Edmund, Æthelred and the shorter tracts, Wl lad, Wl art — probably not from Quadr — Quadr II Praef., CHn cor, Quadr II 4–18, Hn com); another hand adds Instituta Cnuti (related to Cb), then Marbod's poems on stones. It contains the texts Andreas Horn added to Co from a 'Liber S. Augustini Cant.', so Liebermann thinks T belonged to St Augustine's, Canterbury; Sir Simonds d'Ewes either owned T or a sister manuscript, from which Somner cited VII Atr and Iudex and Harley 596 was copied (exemplar called 'pervetusta').

wormald.other_contents: By the 14th century set between Geoffrey of Monmouth and pseudo-historical pieces incl. 'Prester John's' letter to Emperor Manuel; legal section originally distinct (p. 238).
wormald.overview: A Quadripartitus copy of about 1200, later at St Augustine's, Canterbury, representing the fourth of the five stages Wormald identifies, before the final M/Hk arrangement (it still places III Edmund and the run of texts that begins with Alfred–Guthrum and ends with Wergeld differently). By the fourteenth century it had been bound up with Geoffrey of Monmouth's history and other tales of wonder; its legal part, originally separate, was supplemented with related texts such as the Instituta Cnuti.
wormald.key_quote: T (5), otherwise perhaps the latest manuscript, was also given a historical slant by the fourteenth century (p. 238)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: Liebermann dates T c. 1225, Wormald s. xii/xiii (p. 237) — a modest difference (moved from liebermann_superseded).

notes.text: After Geoffrey of Monmouth, an originally separate volume in two hands of c. 1225: the first writes the Quadripartitus from Arg. 1 (Cnut, Alfred–Ine, Æthelstan, Edgar, Edmund, Æthelred and the shorter tracts, Wl lad, Wl art — probably not from Quadr — Quadr II Praef., CHn cor, Quadr II 4–18, Hn com); another hand adds Instituta Cnuti (related to Cb), then Marbod's poems on stones. It contains the texts Andreas Horn added to Co from a 'Liber S. Augustini Cant.', so Liebermann thinks T belonged to St Augustine's, Canterbury; Sir Simonds d'Ewes either owned T or a sister manuscript, from which Somner cited VII Atr and Iudex and Harley 596 was copied (exemplar called 'pervetusta').

A Quadripartitus copy of about 1200, later at St Augustine's, Canterbury, representing the fourth of the five stages Wormald identifies, before the final M/Hk arrangement (it still places III Edmund and the run of texts that begins with Alfred–Guthrum and ends with Wergeld differently). By the fourteenth century it had been bound up with Geoffrey of Monmouth's history and other tales of wonder; its legal part, originally separate, was supplemented with related texts such as the Instituta Cnuti.

O’Brien (2003): end of the 12th or beginning of the 13th century; with Cb one of the two manuscripts of the full text descended from a common source (O’Brien’s δ; posited by Liebermann as tcb). Liebermann saw the link but his apparatus misses most of the evidence for it. (The T in the Huntingdon part of O’Brien’s family tree is a different manuscript.)
